messages.subject: Import RILs data from Stacks
parts:
Dear all,


I am quite at the beginning of my QTL mapping analysis and already having issues about how to import my data. My mapping population is comprised of 94 RIls (Drosophila). Genotyping was done with ddRAD-Seq, reads were aligned to a reference genome (in scaffolds) and markers were called with the software Stacks. 
As output from Stacks, I have only two options: as F2 or generic (GEN). 

First, I tried reading it in F2 format, which gave me a warning about the length of the scaffolds.
When I assigned the cross type as "riself", I got a warning about invalid genotypes.
Next, I tried reading it in GEN format, warning me about "unexpected genotype codes"...

R code is below and I attached both genotype files (F2 and GEN).

Did someone of you have a similar problem? What am I doing wrong?
Thanks a lot for your answers!!!!!!!

Best,

Annabella

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Import RILs data from Stacks
parts:
The warning about the lengths is to emphasize that the marker positions are in vp, but we're going to want them converted to cM. You could ignore that, though I would suggest rescaling the positions.

I'm a bit confused about your treatment of the data as an F2 and then as riself. The large frequency of heterozygotes seems incompatible with thse being RILs.

The warnings about invalid genotypes...R/qtl can't handle that "GEN" format. 

karl

Dear Karl,

thank you very much for the quick reply! As you maybe realized, I am a bit confused, too.
As far as I can see, the only difference between the two export types F2 and GEN is the formatting.
But if I read in the data directly as RILs, I get the warning below.

The samples are indeed RILs. Intercrossing was done for 5 generations and inbreeding was also done for 5 generations. Apparently, the inbreeding was not enough. However, that is the only data set that I have... 
Omitting all these genotypes with code==3... is this because of the large amount of heterozygotes? In that case, can I work with the data at all? Or is there something else I am doing wrong?

Thank you again very much for your answer!!!!!!

Best,
Annabella

> data3<-read.cross("csvr", "./web_filtered", "geno_file_F2.csv", 
+                 "RIL_phenotype_transposed.csv", genotypes=c("a","b","h"), na.strings="-", 
+                 estimate.map = F, crosstype= "riself")
 --Read the following data:
	 94  individuals
	 7962  markers
	 1  phenotypes
 --Cross type: riself 
Warning messages:
1: In convert2riself(cross) : Omitting 162327 genotypes with code==3.

2: In summary.cross(cross) :
  Some chromosomes > 1000 cM in length; there may be a problem with the genetic map.
  (Perhaps it is in basepairs?)

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Import RILs data from Stacks
parts:
R/qtl can't handle heterozygous genotypes in RILs, and so will omit the hets.

The warning you're getting is because the positions are in bp.
You could convert to Mbp and the warning will go away

data3 <- rescalemap(data3, 1e-6)

I would be uncomfortable omitting 25% of genotypes. I guess I would start by just treating it as an F2. I'm surprised at the amount of heterozygosity after 5 generations of selfing.

karl
